title: A Criterion for Covariance in Complex Sequential Growth Models
version: arXiv:2003.11311v1; doi 10.1088/1361-6382/ab987f. Record inherited from knowledge/csg-quantum/sources.jsonl with coordinator-reviewed locators; not re-read in this task.
section_locator: Sec. 2 (cylinder sets Eqs. (1)-(3); covariant set Eq. (4); proof that no nontrivial event in the finite-stage algebra is covariant); Sec. 2.2 (Eqs. (11)-(16), amplitude covariance condition (a)); Sec. 2.3 (variation Eq. (17), Theorem 2.1); Sec. 3.3 (complex percolation extends only for q in [0,1])
relevance: Gives (i) the statement that no nontrivial finite-stage cylinder event is relabelling-covariant, which is why the stage-n quotient here is a truncation, and (ii) Theorem 2.1, bounded variation iff extension, which identifies the divergence computed here with the known non-extension of complex percolation.
assumptions: C-valued vector measure built multiplicatively along labelled paths; internal temporality; covariance as equality of amplitudes of order-isomorphic labelled nodes; Markov sum rule.
conclusion: Extension to the generated sigma-algebra holds iff the finite-stage measure has bounded variation; complex percolation is non-extending except for q in [0,1].
proof_status: Hand proofs; Claims 3.8-3.9 rely on large-n asymptotics; one case explicitly undecided by the authors. Not reproduced here.
limits: Full-text depth inherited, not re-read in this task. No observer, channel, or detector-probability discussion.
used_for: condition (a) covariance of the amplitude; the interpretation of V_n divergence; the caveat that stage-n covariance is a truncation
